ideas.hypothesis: Firms just below the turnover threshold in the official SME definition receive more government policy support and invest more than firms just above it, and some firms manage their turnover to stay below the threshold.
ideas.test: Regression discontinuity around the turnover cut-off in China's SME classification using industrial enterprise survey data: compare subsidies, tax relief, investment and the density of firms near the threshold (McCrary test).
ideas.disconfirming: No discontinuity in support or investment at the threshold, and no bunching of firms just below it.

ideas.hypothesis: Small growth companies that appoint non-executive directors obtain bank credit on better terms (lower spreads, fewer collateral demands) because outside directors reduce information asymmetry with lenders.
ideas.test: Panel of UK or European private SMEs with board-composition data from company registries linked to loan terms (credit register or survey); event-study around non-executive director appointments.
ideas.disconfirming: Loan spreads and collateral requirements do not improve after non-executive directors are appointed.

ideas.hypothesis: Banks that lend to SMEs mainly through relationship lending have lower non-performing loan ratios on SME portfolios than transaction-based lenders, especially in regions with weak disclosure such as Heilongjiang.
ideas.test: Bank-branch level data from regional banks in Northeast China: regress SME NPL ratios on relationship-lending proxies (relationship length, number of banks per borrower, branch distance), with region and year fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: Relationship-lending intensity is unrelated or positively related to SME NPL ratios.

ideas.hypothesis: Introducing punitive damages for intellectual property infringement raises patenting by technology SMEs more than by large firms, because SMEs are less able to protect innovations by other means.
ideas.test: Difference-in-differences using China's legal reforms that introduced punitive damages for IP infringement: compare patent applications by SMEs and large firms before and after, using firm-level patent data.
ideas.disconfirming: SME patenting does not rise relative to large firms after punitive damages are introduced.

ideas.hypothesis: Diffusion of internet banking narrows regional disparities in SME access to innovation loans by reducing dependence on local branch networks.
ideas.test: Repeat the Slovak regional SME survey on innovation loan access with an added question on internet-banking use; compare the regional gap in loan approval between internet-banking users and non-users.
ideas.disconfirming: Regional disparities in loan access are equally large among internet-banking users.

ideas.hypothesis: SMEs with longer and more exclusive bank relationships hold a higher share of long-term debt, which helps explain why short-term financing does not dominate SME capital structure in relationship-based banking systems such as France.
ideas.test: French SME balance sheets (e.g., Banque de France data) linked to number of bank relationships; regress long-term debt share on relationship length and exclusivity, controlling for size, sector and asset tangibility.
ideas.disconfirming: Relationship length and exclusivity have no association with long-term debt share.

ideas.hypothesis: SMEs receiving loans backed by public credit guarantees increase innovation output (patents, new products) relative to comparable non-guaranteed firms, because guarantees relax collateral constraints for intangible-intensive projects.
ideas.test: Matched sample of guaranteed and non-guaranteed SMEs from a guarantee agency's records linked to patent and innovation survey data; propensity-score difference-in-differences over three years.
ideas.disconfirming: Guaranteed firms show no greater increase in innovation output than matched controls.

ideas.hypothesis: Regions with faster and more impartial contract enforcement have higher shares of SME innovation projects financed by bank loans.
ideas.test: Regional cross-section (Slovak or Chinese provinces) relating court efficiency indicators (case duration, enforcement rates) to the share of SME innovation financed by bank credit from firm surveys.
ideas.disconfirming: Enforcement quality has no relation to bank financing of SME innovation.

ideas.hypothesis: SMEs that keep audited or standardized financial records are significantly more likely to obtain bank loans, and the effect is larger where credit information infrastructure is weak.
ideas.test: World Bank Enterprise Survey data for several countries including Bangladesh and China: regress loan approval on audited-statement indicators, interacting with a credit-registry coverage index.
ideas.disconfirming: Audited records do not raise loan approval rates, or the effect does not vary with credit information infrastructure.

ideas.hypothesis: Small companies with independent directors experienced in industry commercialize a higher share of their innovations successfully.
ideas.test: Survey of Czech or UK innovative SMEs combining board composition with the share of sales from new products; regress innovation performance on independent director presence and experience.
ideas.disconfirming: Independent director presence has no association with innovation commercialization.

ideas.hypothesis: During recessions, credit guarantee schemes have larger effects on SME survival and employment than in normal times, because private credit tightens more for small firms.
ideas.test: Firm-level records from a national guarantee program spanning 2005-2012: compare survival and employment outcomes of guaranteed vs matched non-guaranteed firms in 2008-2009 versus other years.
ideas.disconfirming: Guarantee effects on survival and employment are no larger during the recession.

ideas.hypothesis: A small set of standardized SME financial indicators predicts loan default substantially better than size and sector alone, supporting the case for a shared SME data repository.
ideas.test: Logistic or machine-learning default model on bank SME loan data with eight standardized financial ratios versus a baseline with size and sector; compare out-of-sample AUROC.
ideas.disconfirming: Financial indicators improve default prediction only marginally over the baseline.

ideas.hypothesis: EU structural fund support for SME innovation narrows regional disparities in innovation financing within member states such as Slovakia.
ideas.test: Regional panel 2007-2018 of EU fund disbursements to SMEs per firm and survey-based innovation finance access; regress the change in regional gaps on fund intensity.
ideas.disconfirming: Regions receiving more EU funding do not converge in innovation financing.

ideas.hypothesis: Tax relief targeted at SMEs increases the commercialization of new products more than the generation of innovations, because it raises after-tax returns on market launch.
ideas.test: Firm-level innovation survey before and after an SME tax reform (e.g., raised tax thresholds); difference-in-differences on new-product sales share vs innovation incidence for eligible and ineligible firms.
ideas.disconfirming: Tax relief raises neither commercialization nor innovation incidence, or only the latter.

ideas.hypothesis: SMEs absorb more labor per unit of capital than large firms but at lower job quality, so regions relying on SME-led employment growth show lower average job quality.
ideas.test: Linked employer-employee or labor force survey data by firm size: compare employment elasticities and job-quality indices (wages, contracts, safety) across firm sizes and regions.
ideas.disconfirming: SME jobs show equal job quality to large-firm jobs once worker characteristics are controlled.

ideas.hypothesis: A three-party game between bank, SME and guarantor predicts that partial guarantee coverage leads banks to keep screening, so loans with 50-80% coverage have lower default rates than loans with full coverage.
ideas.test: Loan-level guarantee records with coverage ratios: compare default rates across coverage bands, exploiting policy changes in coverage rules.
ideas.disconfirming: Default rates do not differ, or are lower, under full coverage.

ideas.hypothesis: Technology SMEs with stronger management teams (education, prior experience) report fewer financing difficulties at each growth stage.
ideas.test: Survey of firms in a high-tech development zone measuring management team quality and reported financing constraints, by growth stage; ordered logit with stage fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: Management quality is unrelated to reported financing difficulties.

ideas.hypothesis: Provinces that privatized or restructured more state-owned enterprises saw faster growth in bank lending to private SMEs, as credit previously absorbed by SOEs was released.
ideas.test: Provincial panel 1998-2008: regress SME loan growth on the decline in the SOE share of industrial output, using initial SOE share as an instrument.
ideas.disconfirming: SOE reform intensity is unrelated to SME lending growth.

ideas.hypothesis: SME clusters generate positive spillovers to neighbouring counties, so county growth depends on the SME cluster density of neighbouring counties as well as its own.
ideas.test: Spatial Durbin model on county-level data (e.g., Hebei or Beijing region) relating GDP growth to own and neighbours' SME cluster density.
ideas.disconfirming: Neighbours' cluster density has no significant effect on county growth.

ideas.hypothesis: The 2008 financial crisis shifted SME capital structure toward internal equity and trade credit, with larger shifts for SMEs that relied on short-term bank debt before the crisis.
ideas.test: Balance-sheet panel of SMEs (e.g., French or Chinese firms) 2005-2012: difference-in-differences on equity and trade-credit shares by pre-crisis short-term debt reliance.
ideas.disconfirming: No change in capital structure after 2008, or no difference by pre-crisis debt structure.

ideas.hypothesis: Manufacturing SMEs in industries with larger tariff cuts after China's WTO accession increased labor productivity more than SMEs in protected industries.
ideas.test: Chinese industrial enterprise survey 1998-2007: regress SME labor productivity growth on industry-level tariff reductions, with firm and year fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: Tariff cuts have no or negative effects on SME productivity.

ideas.hypothesis: The Western Development Strategy reduced SME financing difficulties in western counties relative to similar central counties, by expanding local banking capacity.
ideas.test: County-level panel 1995-2010 of SME loans and bank branch counties, difference-in-differences comparing western and central counties near the policy border.
ideas.disconfirming: Western counties show no relative improvement in SME credit after 2000.

ideas.hypothesis: Technology SMEs with flatter organizational structures commercialize innovations faster (shorter time from development to market).
ideas.test: Survey of technology SMEs recording hierarchy levels and time-to-market of recent innovations; regression with industry controls.
ideas.disconfirming: Hierarchy depth is unrelated to time-to-market.

ideas.hypothesis: Local governments facing higher employment pressure expand credit guarantee systems for SMEs more rapidly.
ideas.test: Prefecture-level panel of guarantee institution capital and registered unemployment rates, 2003-2015, with lagged unemployment as the main regressor.
ideas.disconfirming: Guarantee expansion is unrelated to local employment pressure.

ideas.hypothesis: SMEs integrated as suppliers into large corporations' supply chains show higher innovation performance than independent SMEs.
ideas.test: SME innovation survey data with a supplier-status question; propensity-matched comparison of new-product sales share.
ideas.disconfirming: Supplier SMEs show no higher innovation performance than matched independent SMEs.

ideas.hypothesis: SMEs participating in regional development programs grow faster in employment and turnover than comparable non-participants, with larger effects in resource-dependent regions.
ideas.test: Program participant lists from a regional program (e.g., Khanty-Mansiysk 2014-2020) matched to business register data; difference-in-differences with matched controls.
ideas.disconfirming: Participants grow no faster than matched non-participants.

ideas.hypothesis: Bangladeshi SMEs with longer bank relationships face fewer of the finance-related growth constraints identified in surveys.
ideas.test: Add relationship-length questions to an SME constraint survey in Bangladesh and regress finance-constraint factor scores on relationship length.
ideas.disconfirming: Relationship length does not reduce finance constraint scores.

ideas.hypothesis: SMEs adopting internet banking reduce financial transaction and administrative operating costs relative to non-adopters.
ideas.test: Panel of SMEs from bank client records or enterprise surveys measuring adoption dates and administrative cost shares; event study around adoption.
ideas.disconfirming: No reduction in operating costs after adoption.

ideas.hypothesis: During economic recessions SMEs shed employment less than large firms, cushioning aggregate unemployment.
ideas.test: Firm-size-class employment data over the 2008-2009 recession across several countries; compare employment changes by size class.
ideas.disconfirming: SMEs shed employment proportionally more than large firms.

ideas.hypothesis: Regions where SMEs have better access to innovation financing grow faster over the following five years.
ideas.test: Regional panel combining survey-based SME innovation financing access with subsequent GDP growth, controlling for initial income and industry structure.
ideas.disconfirming: Innovation financing access does not predict subsequent regional growth.
